cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is writing to the believers in Rome, and he's just told them that where sin increased, grace increased all the more. So he asks the question I bet somebody's already thinking: "Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase?" That's like hearing my oven never burns a batch and asking, so I can just leave the cookies in there FOREVER?

cards.question: True or false: Paul says believers should keep on sinning so that grace can increase.
Paul gives a hard no to sinning so grace can increase. What reason does he give for why believers can't keep living in sin?

cards.text: Paul says, "Certainly not!" Going back to living in sin is like me asking to move back into the junk drawer, and friend, I am NOT going back in there.

cards.question: Then Paul brings up baptism. He says everyone who was baptized into Christ Jesus was baptized into His ___.

cards.text: So Paul says we were buried with Him through baptism into death. Buried sounds like the end, but friend, I thought the back of a drawer was the end too.

cards.question: Believers were buried with Christ through baptism into death. Just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, what may they do?
True or false: Paul says believers who have been united with Christ in His death will certainly also be united with Him in His resurrection.

cards.text: Paul says our old self was crucified with Him, so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless. Powerless, like the dead batteries I shared that drawer with, still swearing they had a little charge left.

cards.question: The old self was crucified with Christ. According to Paul, what should believers no longer be?

cards.text: Anyone who has died has been freed from sin, and if we died with Christ, Paul says we believe we will also live with Him. Sin can knock all it wants, friend, but the old you is NOT answering that door.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says that since Christ was raised from the dead, He can still die again.

cards.text: Death no longer has dominion over Him, and the death He died, He died to sin once for all. Once. For. ALL. No reruns, no sequel, no part two.

cards.question: Christ died to sin once for all, but Paul says the life He lives, He lives to ___.
After all that about Christ, Paul tells the believers how they must count themselves. What does he say they are?

answers.text: Dead to sin but alive to God
Stronger than sin and pleasing to God
Hiding from sin and waiting on God

cards.text: Paul says, "Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body so that you obey its desires." Sin doesn't get the throne, friend, and it doesn't even get a parking spot.

cards.question: Paul tells believers not to present the parts of their body to sin as instruments of ___ but to present them to God as instruments of ___.

cards.text: Paul says to present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life, which is a LOT like going from a junk drawer to a bakery. Then he makes a promise: sin shall not be your master.

cards.question: Paul promises believers that sin shall not be their master. What reason does he give?

answers.text: They are under grace not law
They have kept the whole law

findings.problem: This story card comes after cards 2 and 3 have already asked about Romans 6:2, and it retells the same verse ("Certainly not!"). It adds nothing new to the passage, so it works as a recap instead of moving the baker forward. The junk-drawer joke could ride on a card that tells new material, or the Romans 6:2 telling could come before cards 2 and 3 without giving the answer away.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The wrong words (comfort, silence, leisure) aren't believable for either blank. 'Wickedness' is the only negative word, so it obviously fills the sin blank. That leaves 'righteousness' as the only word that fits the God blank. The right answers stand out, and the card can be solved without reasoning about the verse's meaning.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
